To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a novel plant-specific protein, cpSRP43, is involved in chloroplast protein targeting to the thylakoids.

the Arabidopsis gene encoding cpSRP43 was identified by using a mutant that is defective in chlorophyll a binding antenna proteins and that cpSRP43, a protein with ankyrin and chromodomain motifs, is a novel cpSRP component.
a protein encoded by a gene designated CAO is the cpSRP component that is involved in LHCP targeting and is unique to plants.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of a novel chloroplast signal recognition pathway, which involves a plant-specific protein, cpSRP43, that is involved in LHCP targeting.
the characterization of a new component of the cpSRPs that appears to be specific to plants and is involved in the targeting of LHCP to the thylakoids.
the identification and characterization of a novel chloroplast SRP component that plays a specific role in chloroplast biogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CAO gene encodes an essential component of a plant-specific cpSRP system that is involved in LHCP targeting.
cpSRP43 (CAO) is involved in LHCP targeting and is a plant-specific component of the cpSRPs.
the chaos phenotype is due to a mutation in a gene encoding a plant-specific component of the cpSRPs, which is involved in LHCP targeting.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Arabidopsis chloroplast signal recognition pathway contains at least three components (SRP54, cpSRP43 and CAO) and that these components are involved in the targeting and insertion of chloroplast proteins into the thylacoid membrane.
cpSRP43, a plant-specific protein, is involved in targeting LHCPs to thylakoids.

the cpSRP complex is composed of at least two components, one of which (cpSRP54) is conserved in eukaryotes and prokaryotes, while the other component (cpSRP 43) is plant-specific and may be involved in the targeting of nuclear-encoded chloroplast proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the plant cpSRP system is more complex than previously thought, and that the cpSRP system of Arabidopsis contains at least four components, two of which, cpSRP43 and cpSRP54, are encoded in the nucleus and two of which, FtsY and the 54-kD chloroplast ribosomal protein, are encoded in chloroplasts.
the plant cpSRP system is more complex than the one in other kingdoms.
cpSRP43 and cpSRP54 have different roles in the cpSRP pathway, and cpSRP43 plays a role in LHCP targeting into the thylaokid membrane.
